sample_unit: benchmark questions across nine MultiMedQA subsets

links.outcome: Benchmark accuracy with vs without retrieval-augmented generation grounding in open medical references
links.effect: RAG gave a modest additional accuracy gain of +0.4 points on average, varying by dataset. EHR fine-tuning gave +17.8 points over the base model.
links.quote: EHR-based fine-tuning accounts for the majority of the performance gain (+17.8 percentage points over the base model on average), while RAG provides a modest additional benefit (+0.4 points on average) that varies by dataset.

unlisted_practices: Fine-tuning an LLM on de-identified EHR data to improve accuracy
Quantized on-premises/local deployment for low latency and data-flow control
Qualitative error taxonomy of incorrectly answered benchmark items

screen.reason: The study conducts benchmark evaluations and an ablation study specifically comparing the model with and without retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounding on medical benchmarks.
